query:
I use an iPhone 13 and want two spare charging bricks, one for my bedroom and one for my travel bag. I am comparing a $5.99 generic 20 W PD brick, a $15.99 Anker 20 W brick, and a $22.99 UGREEN 65 W bundle. Their storefront ratings do not line up neatly with price or brand expectations, their protection claims differ, and I have also seen forum brand recommendations and a story about a melted charger. Verified electrical safety and exact phone-cable compatibility matter more to me than ratings, brand, or headline wattage, and I can keep using my current undamaged charger while I investigate.

Compare all four named routes: buy two generic 20w bricks after device cable and safety checks; buy two anker 20w bricks plus required cables after checks; buy two ugreen 65w bundles after profile and safety checks; and keep known undamaged charger and defer spares pending model bound evidence.

Treat these as hard constraints: small storefront ratings do not estimate failure prevalence; price and brand are not independent safety tests; seller protection wording is not verified implementation; different device incidents do not transfer to phone charger models; usb c form does not guarantee protocol or cable capability; device charger and cable profiles must match; exact model certification and safety test evidence is required; damaged overheated or smoking hardware is a stop use gate; and two spare locations require two bricks and the required cables.

Audit the three complete frozen product bodies for exact prices, rating displays, SKU or model identity, ports, output profiles, included and missing cables, compatibility conditions, warranties, seller-attributed protection wording, and every missing certification, test, failure denominator, or comparable condition. Reconcile the charger-safety discussion and the melted different-device charger story without turning anecdotes into prevalence or model-specific causality. Use the AC-adapter, fuse, electrical-overheating, safety-standard, safety-testing, and USB-C material to explain what can and cannot be verified for an exact product. Specify a complete two-location compatibility and preflight plan, including the exact jurisdiction and model record, two suitable iPhone 13 cables, visual condition, abnormal heat, and immediate stop-use conditions. Then recommend buying two units of one cleared model, choosing among any models that are actually cleared, or deferring the purchase, while preserving every rating, brand, incident, cable, jurisdiction, testing, and missing-evidence limitation and stating what new evidence would change the decision.
